message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the development of a mane in adult males. The presence of a mane is controlled by a dominant allele (often referred to as “M”) that overrides the recessive allele (“m”) responsible for a lack of mane. Thus, if a lion inherits at least one copy of the dominant “M” allele from either parent, it will develop a mane. This trait is a classic example of dominance in a natural population.
